dedupe_keys.name: integrating agriculture in national adaptation plans nap ag country case study series undp and fao

description: This series of country case studies describes how countries formulated and implemented National Adaptation Plans with a particular emphasis on agriculture, including forestry, livestock and fisheries, and what the joint UNDP and FAO programme Integrating Agriculture in NAPs (NAP-Ag) contributed. The studies read here cover Thailand, Viet Nam and Kenya; the series aims to share experience among policy makers in Asia, Africa and Latin America. They were produced by the NAP-Ag programme, funded by the German environment ministry through the International Climate Initiative; the Viet Nam study of July 2020 was written by Srijita Dasgupta of FAO with Janto Simon Hess of UNDP. Each study draws on interviews with the country coordinator and ministry staff and on country reports, and sets out adaptation planning steps, programme support, links to the Paris Agreement and the Sustainable Development Goals, and lessons. The studies are available free online on the UNDP adaptation site as web pages and PDF downloads; no licence is stated. Caveats: they are programme self-assessments, the Kenya study notes it was too early to assess impacts, and the Thailand page shows only a placeholder date. For simulation it gives worked examples of how agricultural climate risks, such as drought and floods, enter national adaptation planning, useful for designing adaptation scenarios for food systems. It is related to the USDA Climate Hubs adaptation workbook case studies record in this catalogue.
